arxiv-2105-03837.title: Exploring Bell nonlocality of quantum networks with stabilizing and logical operators
arxiv-2105-03837.creator: Li-Yi Hsu, Ching-Hsu Chen
arxiv-2105-03837.description: Abstract In practical quantum networks, a variety of multiqubit stabilized states emitted from independent sources are distributed among the agents, and the correlations across the entire network can be derived from each agent’s local measurements on the shared composite quantum systems.

arxiv-2110-10479.creator: V. Ryzhii ∗1,2 , M. Ryzhii 3 , A. Satou 1 , V. Mitin 4 , M. S. Shur 5 , and T. Otsuji 1
arxiv-2110-10479.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by V. Ryzhii ∗1,2 , M. Ryzhii 3 , A. Satou 1 , V. Mitin 4 , M. S. Shur 5 , and T. Otsuji 1. Keywords: graphene field-effect transistor, graphene lateral diode, ballistic electrons, electron drag We analyze the operation of the graphene n + -i-n-n + field-effect transistors (GFETs) and lateral diodes (GLDs) with the injection of ballistic electrons into the n-region.

arxiv-2206-13623.title: Learning Controllable 3D Level Generators
arxiv-2206-13623.creator: Zehua Jiang, Sam Earle, Michael Cerny Green, Julian Togelius
arxiv-2206-13623.description: Abstract . Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning ( PCGRL ) foregoes the need for large human-authored data-sets and allows agents to train explicitly on functional constraints, using computable, user-defined measures of quality instead of target output. We explore the application of PCGRL to 3D domains, in which content-generation tasks naturally have greater complexity and potential pertinence to real-world applications.

arxiv-2211-09084.title: Technical Report on Neural Language Models and Few-Shot Learning for Systematic Requirements Processing in MDSE
arxiv-2211-09084.creator: Vincent Bertram, Miriam Boß, Evgeny Kusmenko, Imke Helene Nachmann, Bernhard Rumpe, Danilo Trotta, Louis Wachtmeister
arxiv-2211-09084.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vincent Bertram, Miriam Boß, Evgeny Kusmenko, Imke Helene Nachmann, Bernhard Rumpe, Danilo Trotta, Louis Wachtmeister. Systems engineering, in particular in the automotive domain, needs to cope with the massively increasing numbers of requirements that arise during the development process. To guarantee a high product quality and make sure that functional safety standards such as ISO26262 are fulfilled, the exploitation of potentials of model-driven systems engineering in the form of automatic analyses, consistency checks, and tracing mechanisms is indispensable.

arxiv-2211-15579.title: Patterns in transitional shear turbulence. Part 2: Emergence and optimal wavelength
arxiv-2211-15579.creator: Sébastien Gomé 1, Laurette S. Tuckerman 1, Dwight Barkley 2
arxiv-2211-15579.description: Abstract Low Reynolds number turbulence in wall-bounded shear flows en route to laminar flow takes the form of oblique, spatially-intermittent turbulent structures. In plane Couette flow , these emerge from uniform turbulence via a spatiotemporal intermittent process in which localised quasi-laminar gaps randomly nucleate and disappear. For slightly lower Reynolds numbers, spatially periodic and approximately stationary turbulent-laminar patterns predominate.

arxiv-2412-12218.title: Accelerating Sparse Graph Neural Networks with Tensor Core Optimization
arxiv-2412-12218.creator: Ka Wai Wu
arxiv-2412-12218.description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) have seen extensive application in domains such as social networks, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. However, the irregularity and sparsity of graph data challenge traditional computing methods, which are insufficient to meet the performance demands of GNNs.

arxiv-2503-21286.title: Use of copula functions in error assessment due to deviation from dependence assumption
arxiv-2503-21286.creator: Subarna Bhattacharjee, Aninda Kumar Nanda , Subhashree Patra
arxiv-2503-21286.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyze the relative errors in various reliability measures due to the tacit assumption that the components associated with a n n -component series system or a parallel system are independently working where the components are dependent. We use Copula functions in said error analysis.

arxiv-2506-10449.title: A note on the properties of the confidence set for the local average treatment effect obtained by inverting the score test
arxiv-2506-10449.creator: Ezequiel Smucler, Ludovico Lanni, David Masip
arxiv-2506-10449.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ezequiel Smucler, Ludovico Lanni, David Masip. We study the properties of the score confidence set for the local average treatment effect in non and semiparametric instrumental variable models. This confidence set is constructed by inverting a score test based on an estimate of the nonparametric influence function for the estimand, and is known to be uniformly valid in models that allow for arbitrarily weak instruments; because of this, the confidence set can have infinite diameter at some laws.

arxiv-2509-22818.title: Can Large Language Models Develop Gambling Addiction?
arxiv-2509-22818.creator: Seungpil Lee, Donghyeon Shin, Yunjeong Lee, Sundong Kim
arxiv-2509-22818.description: Abstract This study explores whether large language models can exhibit behavioral patterns similar to human gambling addictions. As LLMs are increasingly utilized in financial decision-making domains such as asset management and commodity trading, understanding their potential for pathological decision-making has gained practical significance. We systematically analyze LLM decision-making at cognitive-behavioral and neural levels based on human gambling addiction research.

arxiv-2510-11753.title: An Effective Method for Solving a Class of Transcendental Diophantine Equations

pmc-13242695.title: Workload, Mental Health and Healthcare Among Academics in Australia: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13242695.creator: Elisa Zentveld, Huy V. Nguyen, Maxwell Winchester, Stephen L. Edwards, Alan Labas, Fadi Charchar

pmc-13427340.title: Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification for A Fractional-Order Model of the Human Ear
pmc-13427340.creator: Prakash KC, Maryam Naghibolhosseini, Mohsen Zayernouri
pmc-13427340.description: We employ the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm to estimate model parameters and quantify their uncertainties in a fractional-order lumped-element model of the human ear in a Bayesian inference framework. The model, originally developed by Naghibolhosseini and Long (2018), incorporates fractional-order elements to capture viscoelastic memory effects in ear tissues that otherwise cannot adequately be represented via conventional integer-order models.
